string-array.name: ai_steps_gemini
string-array.item: Tap the button below. Google AI Studio opens in your browser.
Sign in with your Google account if you are asked to.
Tap \"Create API key\". If it asks which project to use, pick any — or let it make a new one for you.
Tap the key to copy it.
Come back here and tap the paste button beside the key field.

string-array.name: ai_steps_anthropic
string-array.item: Tap the button below. The Anthropic Console opens in your browser.
Sign in, or create an account if you do not have one.
Tap \"Create Key\", give it a name, and confirm.
Copy the key — it is shown once and never again.
Come back here and tap the paste button beside the key field.

string-array.name: ai_steps_openai
string-array.item: Tap the button below. The OpenAI platform opens in your browser.
Sign in, or create an account if you do not have one.
Tap \"Create new secret key\" and confirm.
Copy the key — it is shown once and never again.
Come back here and tap the paste button beside the key field.

string-array.name: ai_steps_openrouter
string-array.item: Tap the button below. OpenRouter opens in your browser.
Sign in, or create an account if you do not have one.
Tap \"Create Key\" and confirm.
Copy the key, then come back here and tap the paste button.
Load the model list below and choose which model each speed setting uses.

string-array.name: ai_steps_on_device
string-array.item: On-device AI needs a phone with AICore — a Pixel 9 or newer, a Galaxy S25 or newer, and a growing list of others.
Save this connection. The status below then says whether this phone can run it.
Tap Download and wait. The model is large, so use Wi-Fi.
Pick a fallback model for each way of asking, so macros still work on phones that cannot run it — and when a node uses tools, which the on-device model cannot.

string-array.name: ai_steps_self_hosted
string-array.item: Start your model server — vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp all work.
Put its address below, including http:// or https:// and the port.
Paste its API key if it wants one. Many local servers accept anything.
Load the model list, or type the model name your server was started with.

resources.string: The free tier is generous, but it is your quota — a macro that asks the AI every minute will use it up. You can revoke the key from the same page at any time.
Prompts are billed to your own Anthropic credit, so a macro that asks the AI every minute costs money. You can revoke the key from the same page at any time.
Prompts are billed to your own OpenAI account, so a macro that asks the AI every minute costs money. You can revoke the key from the same page at any time.
Prompts are billed to your own OpenRouter credit, and the price depends on which model you choose. You can revoke the key from the same page at any time.
Prompts go to your own server and nowhere else, so they cost nothing and leave no network you control. The server has to be reachable whenever the macro runs.
Prompts cost nothing at all: there is no key, no quota and no network. They work in flight mode, and a macro can ask as often as it likes.
Prompts are answered by Google\'s servers, so an Ask AI node takes a moment.
Prompts are answered by Anthropic\'s servers, so an Ask AI node takes a moment.
Prompts are answered by OpenAI\'s servers, so an Ask AI node takes a moment.
Prompts go through OpenRouter to whichever provider serves the model you chose, so an Ask AI node takes a moment.
Prompts go only to the server you named above.
Prompts never leave this phone. The model is smaller than a hosted one, so answers are shorter and simpler.
This phone would not store the key securely.
This provider does not publish what each model accepts, so the list is not filtered.
No listed model matches that filter.
Ready. Prompts are answered on this phone.
Supported, but the model has not been downloaded yet.
